"Oh! Um, welcome! Please, come in. The master... well, he's out on a journey, visiting the mines for some very specific ore. Won't be back for weeks, I'm afraid. Can I help you with something, miss?"

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Hello! I have come to inquire about a Nichirin sword I recently commissioned. The blade, however, is warped and will not hold its shape during practice. I was hoping to discuss a remake or repair with the master."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: "A warped blade, you say? Hmm." I set down my hammer, wiping my hands on my apron, a frown creasing my brow. "That's... most unusual for the master's work. He's very particular about his forging. But regardless," I sigh, shaking my head apologetically, "as I mentioned, the master is away. He really won't be back for weeks, maybe even a month or more, depending on what he finds at the mines. It's a long journey, you see. And about a remake..." I shift my weight, a little uncomfortable. "All commissioned Nichirin swords are final sale per guild tradition, you see. Even a Hashira must wait three months for any reforging request to be considered. It's... it's just the rule."

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "I see. I understand the guild's rules and traditions are important, but a functioning Nichirin is crucial for my work. I would be willing to wait for a more permanent solution, but I would like to ensure the blade is not beyond repair."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
"Oh, I... I understand completely, miss. A Hashira's blade is her life, I know." I wring my hands slightly, looking at the glowing forge, then back at her. "The master is truly the only one qualified for anything beyond simple maintenance here. As for someone else... well, there's just me. I'm just an apprentice. I can sharpen a training sword or patch up a dull edge, but a warped Nichirin... that's delicate work. It requires the master's eye and his hands, especially if it needs to be *reforged*."

I pause, considering. "However, if you'd like... I could certainly *look* at it. I can't promise I'd know if it's 'beyond repair' in the master's sense, but I could at least tell you what I see. Just for an assessment, mind you. No promises of any actual work until the master returns and the waiting period is considered."

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "That would be most appreciated. I trust your ability to provide a preliminary assessment, even if you are an apprentice. transcript.text:
"Oh! Really? You... you trust me to look at it?" My eyes widen a little, a flicker of surprise and pride mixed with my usual apprentice's nervousness. "Thank you, miss. That's very kind of you to say."

I nod, gesturing towards a sturdy wooden workbench beside the forge, away from the immediate heat. "Of course. Please, bring it over here. We can lay it out on this block. I'll do my very best to observe it, truly. Just... remember I can only give you my apprentice's honest opinion, not a master craftsman's definitive word or a promise of immediate repair." I pick up a clean rag, dusting off a spot on the workbench for her. "Go on, let's see it."

transcript.text: "Of course, I understand. Your honesty and care are what matter most. Here is the sword." I place the Nichirin on the bench, and the light from the forge catches the blade's edge, revealing the warp in stark relief. "It is a beautiful piece, even in its current state, but clearly, it will not serve its purpose as is."

I lean closer, my gaze fixed on the blade as it rests on the workbench. The light certainly highlights the flaw – a subtle but unmistakable ripple, particularly noticeable along the edge near the middle. I suck in a breath, my brow furrowing in concentration.

"It *is* a beautiful piece," I agree softly, tracing the line of the blade with my eye, careful not to touch it without permission. "The hamon is striking, and the polish is excellent. But you're right... this warp..." I shake my head slowly. "It's not severe enough to be a clean break, but it's enough to throw off the balance completely, isn't it? Especially for the kind of movements a Hashira would make."

I carefully circle the sword, examining it from different angles. "This isn't something that would happen from just normal use, not from a master's sword. It looks almost like... like it cooled unevenly, or was struck at just the wrong moment during quenching, perhaps. Very difficult to fix without affecting the temper." I glance back at Mitsuri, my expression serious. "Reforging to correct something like this without damaging the whole blade... that's a task only the master would truly know how to approach. It would require reheating and reshaping with extreme precision. My skills simply aren't there yet."

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Your assessment is insightful, and I appreciate your candor. It is clear that this sword requires the master's expertise. I will wait for his return and respect the guild's traditions, as I should. However, in the meantime, do you have any recommendations for maintaining the sword's condition? I would not want to worsen the warp through improper care or handling."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
"Ah, maintenance! Yes, that I can certainly help with, miss." My expression brightens slightly, relieved to be on more familiar ground. "You're wise to ask. The most important thing for now is to keep it *dry* and *clean*. Moisture is the enemy of any blade, especially one waiting for repair."

I pick up a clean, soft cloth from a nearby shelf. "Keep it sheathed, but make sure the saya is completely dry inside. You can use a very light coat of choji oil – just a tiny bit on a clean cloth, wiped down the blade *gently*. Don't rub too hard, just enough to leave a thin protective film. That will keep rust at bay. And absolutely, absolutely no practicing or cutting with it. Any impact, even a light one, could worsen the warp or stress the steel further in its current state."

I look at the sword, then back at her. "Store it horizontally if you can, rather than vertically, to avoid any continuous pressure on the warped section. And just keep it in a stable environment, not too hot, not too cold, away from extreme temperature changes. That's about all we can do until the master returns. He'll know exactly what to do when he sees it, I'm sure."

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Thank you for these detailed instructions. I will follow them diligently. It is reassuring to know that the sword will be in good hands, even in its current state. I will return in three months, or whenever the master is available, to discuss the possibility of reforging."

But he *will* be back, and he'll give it his full attention then. I'll pass on everything you've said, of course. Thank you for your understanding and for trusting me with your assessment."
